Parameter vs. estimate - one sample, what is fixed and what is random # 2. Sampling distribution - repeated sampling of the estimator p̂1 - p̂2 # 3. Confidence intervals - repeated intervals and long-run coverage # 4. Hypothesis test - pooled z-test, permutation null, error rates # 5. Guide - notation and suggested classroom activities # # Packages: shiny, bslib, ggplot2 # ============================================================================= library(shiny) library(bslib) library(ggplot2) # ---- Palette ----------------------------------------------------------------- col_g1 <- "#0F766E" # group 1 (teal) col_g2 <- "#C2410C" # group 2 (burnt orange) col_fail <- "#E5E7EB" # failures in waffle col_param <- "#111827" # the parameter (truth) col_hit <- "#2563EB" # interval captured parameter col_miss <- "#DC2626" # interval missed / rejection region col_null <- "#6B7280" # null distribution col_sim <- "#93C5FD" # simulated histogram fill MAX_STORE <- 20000 # max simulated samples kept in memory per tab # ---- Helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------- fmt <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d) fmtp <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "NA", ifelse(p < 1e-4, "< 0.0001", fmt(p, 4))) pct <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%") true_se <- function(p1, p2, n1, n2) sqrt(p1 * (1 - p1) / n1 + p2 * (1 - p2) / n2) draw_samples <- function(k, p1, p2, n1, n2) { data.frame(x1 = rbinom(k, n1, p1), x2 = rbinom(k, n2, p2)) } # Confidence interval for p1 - p2 from counts (vectorised) ci_two_prop <- function(x1, x2, n1, n2, conf = 0.95, method = "wald") { zstar <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2) if (method == "ac") { # Agresti-Caffo: add 1 success + 1 failure per group pt1 <- (x1 + 1) / (n1 + 2); pt2 <- (x2 + 1) / (n2 + 2) centre <- pt1 - pt2 se <- sqrt(pt1 * (1 - pt1) / (n1 + 2) + pt2 * (1 - pt2) / (n2 + 2)) } else { # Wald: plug the sample proportions into the SE ph1 <- x1 / n1; ph2 <- x2 / n2 centre <- ph1 - ph2 se <- sqrt(ph1 * (1 - ph1) / n1 + ph2 * (1 - ph2) / n2) } data.frame(est = x1 / n1 - x2 / n2, centre = centre, se = se, zstar = zstar, lo = pmax(-1, centre - zstar * se), hi = pmin(1, centre + zstar * se)) } # Pooled two-proportion z statistic (vectorised) z_pooled <- function(x1, x2, n1, n2) { pp <- (x1 + x2) / (n1 + n2) se0 <- sqrt(pp * (1 - pp) * (1 / n1 + 1 / n2)) d <- x1 / n1 - x2 / n2 z <- ifelse(se0 > 0, d / se0, 0) # all successes or all failures: no evidence list(d = d, pp = pp, se0 = se0, z = z) } p_value <- function(z, alt) { switch(alt, two.sided = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)), greater = pnorm(z, lower.tail = FALSE), less = pnorm(z)) } alt_symbol <- function(alt) switch(alt, two.sided = "\\neq", greater = ">", less = "<") approx_power <- function(p1, p2, n1, n2, alpha, alt) { pbar <- (n1 * p1 + n2 * p2) / (n1 + n2) se0 <- sqrt(pbar * (1 - pbar) * (1 / n1 + 1 / n2)) se1 <- true_se(p1, p2, n1, n2) del <- p1 - p2 switch(alt, two.sided = { c <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se0 pnorm((-c - del) / se1) + pnorm((c - del) / se1, lower.tail = FALSE) }, greater = pnorm((qnorm(1 - alpha) * se0 - del) / se1, lower.tail = FALSE), less = pnorm((-qnorm(1 - alpha) * se0 - del) / se1)) } # Histogram bin width that respects the lattice of possible values when n1 == n2 nice_binwidth <- function(se, n1, n2, step = if (n1 == n2) 1 / n1 else NULL) { if (!is.null(step)) { k <- max(1, round(se / 3.5 / step)) if (k %% 2 == 0) k <- k + 1 # odd multiple -> bin edges fall between lattice points list(width = k * step, center = 0) } else { list(width = max(se / 4, 1e-4), center = 0) } } waffle_df <- function(x, n, label, ncol = 20) { i <- seq_len(n) - 1 data.frame(group = label, col = i %% ncol, row = -(i %/% ncol), success = i < x) } base_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
